card.title: Jewish American Security Act

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Jewish American Security Act aims to strengthen federal efforts to counter antisemitism and protect the Jewish community through measures involving education, security grants, threat assessments, and online platform transparency.

affected_groups.effect: Receive increased federal protection, security resources, threat monitoring, and efforts to combat antisemitism in schools, communities, and online.
affected_groups.group: Jewish community members and Jewish Americans

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new Title VI awareness, training, coordinator, grievance, and reporting requirements administered by the Department of Education.
affected_groups.group: Students and educational institutions receiving federal financial assistance

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for expanded security grant funding and law enforcement support for physical security and protection.
affected_groups.group: Nonprofit organizations and houses of worship

affected_groups.effect: May receive grants for increased policing presence and patrols at houses of worship, and must process nonprofit grant reimbursement requests within 90 days.
affected_groups.group: State and local law enforcement agencies

affected_groups.effect: Required to submit and publish detailed periodic transparency reports on their content moderation practices regarding antisemitic content under FTC enforcement.
affected_groups.group: Large online platforms with at least 50 million unique monthly users

key_provisions: Establishes training, public awareness campaigns, written reminders, an antisemitism coordinator, and a Title VI clearinghouse within the Department of Education.
Requires schools receiving federal funds to designate a Title VI coordinator, adopt nondiscrimination policies and grievance procedures, and maintain relevant records.
Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require the disaggregation of campus crime statistics by bias category and bias motivation.
Increases authorization of appropriations for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program to $1,000,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 and modifies grant administration rules.
Authorizes the Attorney General to award grants to state and local law enforcement agencies to support increased policing presence, patrols, and training for houses of worship.

Requires the FBI, Department of Homeland Security, and National Counterterrorism Center to jointly produce annual domestic and transnational threat assessments regarding antisemitic violent extremism.
Mandates that large online platforms publish regular transparency reports on their content moderation practices regarding antisemitic content, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact criteria the FTC will use for rulemaking under Section 6.
Detailed criteria on how individual state reimbursement reviews under the Nonprofit Security Grant Program will handle exceptions requiring additional documentation.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Jewish American Security Act aims to strengthen federal efforts to counter antisemitism and protect the Jewish community through measures involving education, security grants, threat assessments, and online platform transparency.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a broad, multi-agency federal effort to address antisemitism by combining educational civil rights enforcement, increased funding for physical security grants, coordinated intelligence threat assessments, and mandatory transparency reporting for major online platforms.
